title: A Gentle Goodbye to the Screen: A Tear-Free Routine
summary:
Imagine this scene: your child is engrossed in their small digital world, eyes eagerly following cartoons, and suddenly it's time to turn off the screen. The usual tantrum begins—screaming, crying, clinging to the device as if their life depends on it. You feel exhausted and wonder: Am I the only one going through this? Is there another way to end screen time without these daily battles?

What's happening with your child isn't a challenge to you personally; it's a natural part of their development. At this age, children are still developing their self-control and their ability to transition smoothly between activities. For them, turning off the screen means a sudden end to great fun, without yet having the internal tools to cope with this shift. They don't understand the logic; instead, they feel a loss, and this feeling often translates into anger.

The key is preparation and a calm routine. Instead of a sudden shutdown, give your child clear signals and enough time to prepare. Make the transition to another beloved activity, not to emptiness. Consistently upholding the rule calmly and firmly, while understanding your child's feelings, will gradually reduce the intensity of resistance and make saying goodbye to the screen a smoother experience for everyone.
try_this: Tonight: Five minutes before turning off the screen, give your child a clear warning, then immediately transition to an alternative activity they love (such as reading a story or building blocks).
reflection_prompts: How did your child react when transitioning from the screen to the alternative activity?
What activity seems to make it easier for your child to transition to after screen time?
parent_script: “Five more minutes, my dear, then we’ll play with cars!”
assistant_prompts: What alternative activities can I offer my 4-6 year old after screen time?
How do I handle a tantrum if it occurs despite the prior warning?
